_comment: Source of truth for what is published at https://vizora.cloud/tv and
https://vizora.cloud/downloads/vizora-display.apk.
`candidate` is the artifact verified by scripts/release/verify-display-apk.mjs.
`published` is the artifact currently live (null until the first publish); it is
the baseline the next release's signing certificate, versionCode and compiled
default origins are compared against.
`published` describes what customers are running RIGHT NOW, so it is only ever
updated by promoting a candidate that has actually been published. Never edit it to
make a gate pass — for a deliberate environment move use `originTransition`.
`approval` encodes the two release gates. publish-display-apk.sh REFUSES to run
while either pair is null. Do not fill these in without the named human actually
confirming. Never put the keystore, its password, or any private key in this repo.
_originTransition_comment: Explicit authorisation for a DELIBERATE change of backend environment. Normally
null: a release must be compiled against the same origins as the published one.
Why this exists rather than 'just update the baseline'. published.compiledOrigins
describes the artifact that is CURRENTLY LIVE. Editing it to the new origins so the
gate goes green would falsify the record of what customers are actually running, in
order to authorise a change that has not happened yet — in the one file whose job is
to be true about production. published.compiledOrigins is therefore IMMUTABLE until
the new candidate is actually published, at which point candidate is promoted in the
normal way and this block is cleared.
Shape, when a migration is approved:
"from":       { "api": ..., "realtime": ..., "dashboard": ... },
"to":         { "api": ..., "realtime": ..., "dashboard": ... },
"approvedBy": "<name>",
"approvedAt": "YYYY-MM-DD"
The gate accepts a difference from the published baseline only when `from` matches
the live published origins exactly, `to` matches BOTH the packaged artifact and the
releaseOrigins policy pin, and an approver and date are recorded. Requiring `from`
to match the live baseline makes the authorisation self-invalidating: once the
migration is published, the same block can no longer wave through a second, different
move — it has to be re-approved against the new baseline.

_comment: The backend origins a published Vizora Display APK must be COMPILED WITH as its
defaults. All three are required: the verifier rejects a partial pin, because
comparing only the keys that happen to be present silently drops the rest.
SCOPE — read this before relying on it. This pins BUILD PROVENANCE: which origins
were compiled into the artifact. It is NOT a statement about where a running
device ends up pointed. The client seeds DEFAULT_CONFIG from these values and then
applies URL parameters and stored Preferences, and the guarded update_config path
can move a paired device to another host in the same registrable domain. Effective
runtime destination has its own controls; this check does not cover it and must
not be cited as if it did.
The verifier reads these back OUT OF THE PACKAGED APK — from the
__VIZORA_RELEASE_ORIGINS__ marker the bundle stamps in at build time — and
refuses to publish on mismatch. Everything else in this file describes the
artifact's identity; this describes what it was built to point at, which nothing
checked until vizora-tv#18.
Why it was needed: until 1.3.13 the origins came from a gitignored, machine-local
.env, with a fallback to a DIFFERENT environment (api.vizora.io) when absent. An
APK aimed at the wrong backend has a valid package id, a correct version, the
right certificate and a perfectly good hash — it passed every check we had.
Must stay in lockstep with release-origins.json in the vizora-tv repo, which is
what the build compiles from. Changing one without the other fails the gate,
which is the intended behaviour: the two are a matched pair, and a mismatch means
the build and the publish disagree about where customers are being pointed.
The canonical Vizora Android customer-signing identity.
Every publish — INCLUDING THE FIRST — must produce an APK whose signing
certificate equals canonicalCertSha256. The `published` baseline below only
protects release 2 onward; pinning here is what protects release 1, which is
exactly where the 2026-08-10 mismatch was found.
Pin this ONLY after the key passes full durability verification: private-key
entry exists, certificate SHA-256 known, keystore has a secure off-machine
backup, credentials recoverable by an authorized operator, and restoration
tested well enough to prove the key still signs. Record classification and
ownership only — never a password or private-key material.
signing.backupClass: encrypted (aes-256-cbc/pbkdf2) copy on the company VPS at /opt/secure-backups/vizora/android-signing — dir 700, file 600, root-owned, outside every web, Docker and application root; credentials held separately in an owner-controlled password manager
_findings_2026_08_10: GATE B FAILED. The key that signed vizora-display-1.3.10-release.apk
(cert AA07524A…A5137982, created 2026-03-31) is NOT on the Windows build
machine. The only Android keystore there — vizora-tv android/vizora-release.jks,
single entry, alias vizora-display, created 2026-03-26 — carries a DIFFERENT
certificate: BE2320A5…3A9187A5. Not signed in CI, not the debug key, and no
other .jks/.keystore exists under the user profile or OneDrive.
DO NOT PUBLISH the existing 1.3.10 APK. Once canonicalCertSha256 is pinned to
a durable key, the verifier refuses that binary automatically — its cert will
_status_2026_08_10_evening: 1.3.11 has now been BUILT and fully verified against the on-machine key,
and its certificate is BE2320A5…3A9187A5 — matching the rehearsal candidate
exactly, which independently confirms which key actually signs here.
GATE B IS STILL FAILED, and it is the only thing between this build and
publication. Its two open items are facts about custody, not paperwork:
- no secure OFF-MACHINE backup of the keystore
- no credential recovery independent of this one Windows machine
Neither can be closed by an agent, because neither is a decision — they
require someone to actually place the backup and own the recovery.
Publishing before they are closed is the one irreversible move here: the
risk starts the moment a customer installs, and if the key is then lost
every TV in the field needs uninstall + re-pair to ever update again.
_playStoreNote: Before customer rollout, compare the canonical sideload certificate with the
Google Play App Signing certificate. If they differ, pilot customers migrating
from the sideloaded APK to the Play Store build will need one uninstall +
reinstall (and will re-pair). Document it before the migration, not after.

_comment: Built from source 2026-08-13 on vizora-tv branch release/1.3.13, commit 9efd6ee.
No new functional work. This packages the TV source already merged to master;
the only source delta since the 1.3.12 build commit (538d10b) is fe01cad — the
status bar now hides once the device is online and stays visible for every other
state — plus 031a2a7, which is test-only (.env.test pins the compiled-in VITE_*
defaults so the allowlist suite stops depending on a developer's local .env).
No android/ change beyond the version bump itself, no dependency change.
The 1.3.12 keep-screen-awake fix ships again unchanged and was re-verified in
this binary, not assumed: MainActivity.onCreate -> keepScreenOn() ->
Window.addFlags(0x80) survives R8 in the release dex, and a running install of
this exact APK reports fl=KEEP_SCREEN_ON in dumpsys window.
Installs as an UPDATE over the published 1.3.12 — same certificate, versionCode
10143 > 10142 — so paired screens keep their pairing. Do not uninstall first.
Verified by installing the live 1.3.12 bytes on an Android TV emulator, writing a
marker into /data/data/com.vizora.display/files, then replace-installing this APK:
the marker survived and the app uid was unchanged (10192).

_compiledOrigins_comment: The compiled-in DEFAULT origins read back out of this artifact by the verifier,
recorded here the same way apkSha256 and signingCertSha256 are: a fact about the
bytes, promoted into `published` on publish so it becomes the baseline the next
null for 1.3.13 because that build predates the __VIZORA_RELEASE_ORIGINS__ marker
(vizora-tv#18) — there is genuinely nothing to record, and the verifier reports the
baseline comparison as SKIPPED rather than letting an absent baseline read as a
continuity check that ran and passed. 1.3.14 is the first release that can fill it.
Scope: this is what the build compiled in as defaults, NOT where a device ends up
pointed. URL params, stored Preferences and the guarded update_config path can all
move effective runtime config. This field is build provenance.

_comment: compiledOrigins is null because 1.3.13 predates the __VIZORA_RELEASE_ORIGINS__
marker (vizora-tv#18). It is the release-over-release baseline for the compiled
default origins, so it stays null until a marker-carrying build is published; the
verifier reports that comparison as SKIPPED rather than as a passed check.
LIVE at https://vizora.cloud/tv and /downloads/vizora-display.apk since 2026-08-13.
Published bytes verified against this hash twice: from the server itself, and by
downloading the public URL from an independent network. The /tv page asserts the
same version and the same hash.
Packages the TV source already merged to master — status bar hides once online
(fe01cad) plus test-only 031a2a7 — with no new customer-facing work added to cut
the release. The 1.3.12 keep-screen-awake fix ships again unchanged.
Installed as an UPDATE over 1.3.12 (same certificate, versionCode 10143 > 10142),
so paired screens keep their pairing. Confirmed on an Android TV emulator against
the live 1.3.12 bytes, not inferred from the version rule alone: app data survived
and the app uid was unchanged.
health-guardian's install-surface probe was confirmed reading these bytes at
2026-08-13T02:20:05Z (APK 1250365 bytes, correct MIME, installer page HTTP 200).
SERVICE RESTARTS — what this publish did and did not do. The publish itself
invoked no service restart: publish-display-apk.sh contains no PM2 call and writes
only under /var/www/vizora/. It ran 02:15:08-02:15:24Z.
SEPARATELY, vizora-web WAS restarted at 02:17:20Z — roughly two minutes after the
publish finished — by an external session or process, not by this release. PM2
recorded it as a graceful restart (SIGINT, exit 0), and the restart counter did
not advance. vizora-middleware and vizora-realtime were not restarted at all.
Recorded because an earlier draft of this release record flatly claimed 'no
service restarted', which the same session's own PM2 evidence then contradicted.
The honest statement is narrower and is the one that belongs in a durable record:
the release operation did not restart anything; something else restarted the web
process shortly afterwards. Customer surfaces (/tv, the APK URL and its hash, the
homepage, the API and the realtime handshake) were all revalidated AFTER that
restart and were healthy.
Hardware acceptance remains POST-PUBLICATION: the first customer installation is
the test. See approval._gateA_scope.
This block is the baseline the NEXT release is compared against: its signing
certificate must match, and versionCode must be strictly greater than 10143.
PREVIOUS: 1.3.12, versionCode 10142, apkSha256 1D035BDB…515F8EF7, published
2026-08-11 from commit 538d10b. Its bytes were archived server-side as
vizora-display-1.3.12-release.apk during this publish, after the archive step
confirmed the live file still hashed to the recorded published value.

approval._gateA: Artifact approval — confirm this exact APK is the intended client-pilot build, not merely the newest GitHub prerelease.
_gateA_scope: APPROVED 2026-08-13, bound to apkSha256
C5C0B72C4B3EB15FA08F63F9001FB3CD6CB0361957E601F682179BE50F856C72 and nothing else.
The current Vizora Android release process is not established as byte-reproducible:
we have never demonstrated that rebuilding a given commit yields an identical
binary, so a rebuild must be assumed to VOID this approval. Reset to null and
re-approve if that ever happens. The 1.3.13 build was deliberately run ONCE for
this reason, and nothing was rebuilt after approval.
Stated that way on purpose. The binding is to the artifact hash, and that binding
is what protects customers — it holds whether or not the pipeline turns out to be
reproducible. Do not soften it into a claim about Android in general: if the
process is ever made reproducible and demonstrated as such, the rationale here
changes but the exact-hash binding should stay.
What this approval covers, 1.3.13: the TV source already reviewed and merged to
vizora-tv master, packaged unchanged. Source delta since the 1.3.12 build commit
is fe01cad (status bar hides once online) plus test-only 031a2a7. No new
customer-facing feature was added for this release. Binary facts were verified
mechanically before approval — package, versionName/versionCode, pinned
certificate, cross-scheme apksigner, keep-screen-on flag live in dumpsys, and a
real replace-install over the published 1.3.12 that preserved app data and uid.
PRIOR APPROVAL, superseded: 1.3.12 was approved 2026-08-11 bound to apkSha256
1D035BDBB48720B9BCE1F0C8ADA8E74436E9D37A03D9A11FF7CEFA6B515F8EF7. Its
post-publication pilot terms below carry forward unchanged, because 1.3.13 ships
the same keep-screen-awake implementation.
POST-PUBLICATION PILOT CONFIRMATION — REQUIRED
Publication is distribution-only and does not update existing Android TV
installations. The TV client has NO auto-update path: its command set is
push_content / reload / clear_cache / unpair / update_config plus content types,
none of which installs an APK (electron-updater belongs to the desktop client and
is untouched). Screens already on 1.3.11 stay there unless someone deliberately
installs. That is why this approval could move from pre-publication acceptance to
post-publication confirmation without widening the blast radius: in this window the
only installer is the pilot customer.
Gate A was therefore approved on source, static and binary evidence for a bounded
one-customer pilot. THE FIRST CUSTOMER INSTALLATION IS THE HARDWARE ACCEPTANCE TEST
for screen-awake behaviour.
Outcomes:
- Panel stays awake past its configured timeout -> close the defect.
- Flag present but panel still sleeps -> reopen the OEM POWER-POLICY question
only, NOT this application-layer implementation. FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON cannot
reach an OEM eco/no-signal mode. Do not add WakeLocks speculatively.
Customer instruction: install from vizora.cloud/tv OVER the existing app. Do not
uninstall first — uninstalling wipes app data and forces re-pairing.
Caveat worth knowing: we cannot confirm server-side which build a screen runs.
The TV sends appVersion in every heartbeat, but the gateway never reads it and
nothing writes it to Display.metadata (0 of 23 prod devices have the key), while
the dashboard renders an App Version row that can never populate. Tracked as TV2.
UPDATE 2026-08-11: TV2 is fixed — the heartbeat appVersion is now persisted to
devices.metadata, so future rollouts can be confirmed server-side rather than by asking
the customer. The caveat above stood at the time 1.3.12 was approved.
_artifactApprovedSha256_comment: Gate A's binding, machine-readable. The prose above has always said the approval is
bound to one exact SHA-256 and that a rebuild voids it — but nothing enforced that:
publish only checked artifactApprovedBy was non-null, so an approval recorded for one
binary would have waved through any other. The verifier now requires this to equal
BOTH candidate.apkSha256 and the SHA-256 of the APK actually passed to publish.
Reset to null and re-approve whenever a new artifact is built.
approval._gateB: Signing-key durability — confirm the release keystore has a secure off-machine backup and a recoverable password owned by an authorized operator. Record location CLASS and ownership only, never the key or password.
_gateB_evidence: CLOSED 2026-08-10 (second attempt). Split by who established what, so a future
reader knows which parts are machine-checked and which rest on the owner.
Machine-verified: the encrypted backup was created, uploaded, then RETRIEVED
FROM THE VPS and restored — decrypt produced a file byte-identical to the
original (DB5C23DD…654BC3), which opened as PrivateKeyEntry alias
vizora-display and signed a disposable APK that apksigner verified across
v1+v2+v3 with certificate BE2320A5…3A9187A5. Isolation verified, not assumed:
no nginx root/alias into /opt, no container mount, 4/4 HTTP probes 404. The
original keystore re-hashed unchanged and every temporary copy was shredded.
Ciphertext on the VPS: A666578E…98A725F3, 600, root-owned.
Owner-attested (not machine-checkable, by design): both secrets — the backup
encryption passphrase and the keystore password — were filed in an
owner-controlled password manager and read back before the staging folder was
deleted. Confirmed by Srini 2026-08-10; the deletion was independently
re-checked here and no stray copy remains on the build machine.
Recovery after a total build-machine loss: vault -> passphrase -> decrypt the
VPS copy -> vault -> keystore password -> open. No step depends on the Windows
machine, which is what this gate exists to guarantee.
PRIOR INCIDENT, kept deliberately: this gate was closed and reopened earlier
the same day because the first passphrase was lost, making the first ciphertext
permanently undecryptable. The key was never at risk. The cause was ordering —
the staging folder was deleted before read-back from the vault was confirmed.
Filing a secret is not the same as having it. Re-run the restore drill
periodically; key custody rots quietly and only surfaces when it is expensive.
STILL CLOSED for 1.3.13 (2026-08-13). Nothing about the key or its custody
changed: 1.3.13 is signed by the same certificate BE2320A5…3A9187A5, which the
release gate re-checked against the pin, and no backup location, credential owner
or recovery path moved since 2026-08-10. This gate is about the KEY, not the
artifact, so it does not need re-closing per release — only re-checking that the
key and custody state are unchanged, which they are. The restore drill above has
not been re-run since 2026-08-10 and is the item that will age.
approval.signingKeyLocationClass: encrypted copy on company VPS outside all web/app roots + credentials in an owner-controlled password manager
